behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From the Stage-2 TRAIN split only: scan each training sequence with a forward window of 3 and count directed transitions (i -> j), giving a sparse row-normalised matrix Q (24556 x 24556, one sparse pass, done once before training, frozen into a buffer). behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak

Validation and test sessions are never tokenised into the scan, the frozen buffer is never recomputed from any other split, and N_l and s_l are recomputed only from the train items' own forward passes. Therefore no validation or test interaction can influence a radius, a codeword position, a curvature, or a SID; the Stage-3 evaluation reads the finished SIDs only.

behavioral_evidence.claim: the proposed training-only signal
behavioral_evidence.value: Per-pair directed successor-code transition counts: for each level l, the count of training-split sequences in which an item i with level-(l−1) code k' is immediately followed by an item j whose level-l code is k. The signal is the code-level successor distribution B_l[k',·], used as a row-normalised prior over level-l codes; it is not item popularity, and it is not the item's own context entropy.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From the Stage-2 training split only (the same training user sequences with adjacent timestamps used to form the training items): form the directed multiset of consecutive pairs (i_t → i_{t+1}) with gap 1 inside each user sequence; add the Stage-1 co-consumption pairs only if the baseline already uses them for training items, otherwise not. Once per epoch, run one no-grad forward pass over the 24556 training items' encoder outputs with the current codebook, cache T_l(i) = argmax code at level l, and accumulate B_l[k',k] += 1 for every training pair with T_{l−1}(i)=k' and T_l(j)=k (k'=0 dummy at l=1). The table is frozen for the whole following epoch, is integer-valued, and never carries gradient.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: The transition counts use only interactions from the training split, over the 24556 training items, and only the previous epoch's cached argmax codes of those training items. Validation and test interactions never enter B_l, never enter β_l or τ_l (which are minibatch training statistics), and never enter the codebook or the SID assignment. No Stage-3 label, no test sequence and no validation split item is read during SID construction; Stage 3 consumes the frozen SIDs and interacts with nothing in this mechanism.

geometric_necessity.value: Fixed negative curvature c = −1 in the Poincaré ball: geodesic distance d_H(p,q) = arcosh(1 + 2||p−q||²/((1−||p||²)(1−||q||²))), exponential map at the origin exp_0(v) = tanh(||v||/2)·v/(||v||+1e-8), logarithmic map log_0(p) = 2·artanh(||p||)·p/(||p||+1e-8), and Möbius subtraction a ⊖ b = a ⊕ (−b) with a ⊕ b = ((1+2a·b+||b||²)a + (1−||a||²)b)/(1+2a·b+||a||²||b||²). Curvature is fixed, not trainable; no constant is chosen by search.

In quantisation, at every level of the residual-quantiser chain: the residual and the code tangents are exponentiated into the ball and compared by the geodesic distance in the assignment cost; the same exp_0/log_0 pair defines the decoded code vector for the straight-through reconstruction; and the residual passed to the next level is produced by Möbius subtraction inside that same ball. It also sets the cell size, because the tangent-space normalisation is β_l, the measured residual RMS of that level.

logit_{i,k}^{(l)} = −d_H( exp_0(r_{l−1,i}/β_l), exp_0(U_{l,k}) ) − (1/ln K)·log( K·(B_l[k'_i,k] + 1)/(S_l[k'_i] + K) ), with d_H the arcosh Poincaré distance of curvature −1, B_l[k'_i,·] the training-only successor-code transition counts conditioned on the item's own level-(l−1) code, and β_l the measured residual RMS of level l; the code exponentiated is exactly the code decoded: β_l·log_0(q_{l,k}) = β_l·U_{l,k}.

behavioral_evidence.value: Per-parent-code successor branching entropy of the directed item-transition graph (a behaviour-conditioned per-code measure of how diversely the residents of a parent semantic cell are consumed next), together with the parent's occupancy.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From the training split only: for every training user sequence and every consecutive pair (v_t, v_{t+1}) with v_t != v_{t+1}, increment N[v_t, v_{t+1}] once per user (deduplicated per user so heavy users do not dominate); sparse CSR over the 24556 training items. From the current (detached) assignment snapshot, residents I_{l,m} = items whose level-(l-1) code is m; successor mass s_{m,j} = sum_{i in I} N[i,j]; p_{m,j} = s_{m,j}/sum_j s_{m,j}; aggregate successors into level-1 prefix classes c: q_{m,c} = sum_{j: l1code(j)=c} p_{m,j}; h_{l,m} = H(q)/log K_1 in [0,1]; hbar_l = mean over occupied parents; n_{l,m} = |I_{l,m}|. All three are EMAs updated inside the normal training batches (the sample already yields both the item's code and its next item, so no extra pass).

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: Transitions, occupancies and branching entropies are built exclusively from training-split sequences and from item embeddings learned on the training split; the assignment snapshot is computed on training items only. No validation or test interaction is ever read while constructing the codes, so a validation/test item's identity, popularity or neighbours cannot influence its own or any other item's SID; the validation set is used only for the recorded diagnostics and the test set only for the final Stage-3 recall.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: b_i/pop_i is replaced by the constant 1, so rho_{l,k}=1 for every occupied codeword (empty codewords also get rho=1), kappa_{l,k}=kappa0=1.0638 uniformly, and the geometry remains fully hyperbolic with the same renormalisation and STE; this isolates the behaviour contribution and is coded by one switch BEHAV_OFF=True (not trained in this round).
ideas.ablation_both_on: Full mechanism of this block: renormalised residual shell + per-codeword curvature field from behaviour reach per occupant + Poincare geodesic assignment/commitment + unchanged STE. This is the single run this round performs.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: exp_0/log_0 become identity and D becomes the Euclidean-weighted distance D^E_{l,k}=||z_l - e_{l,k}||*rho_{l,k}^{-1/2}, with c_{l,k}=e_{l,k}, the same STE and the same behaviour table; this isolates curvature and is coded by GEOM_OFF=True (not trained in this round).
ideas.behavior_computation: From TRAIN split sequences only (user histories ordered by time). For each position t and each j in (t, t+5] of the same user history, increment C_{u_t,u_j}; pop_i = training occurrence count (floored at 1). b_i = sum_j C_ij / sqrt(pop_i*pop_j) (popularity-adjusted reach of item i to its successors). Everything is a static table built once before Stage 2 and read-only during training; no validation or test interaction is ever read.
ideas.behavior_signal: Popularity-adjusted directed transition reach of an item, consumed per (level, codeword) as behavioural reach per occupant relative to the level mean.
ideas.cost_estimate: Relative to the frozen Stage-2 baseline: +3 to +5% wall clock, no extra epoch, no extra forward pass. Per step at the frozen scale (24556 items, 24 steps/epoch => about 1023 items/step, 3000 epochs): 3*1023*256 = 786k curvature-specific distance evaluations (each about 20 flops, incl. one acosh), 768 curvature table entries recomputed once per step (detached), and one scatter-add of 3*1023 hard assignments into occ/phi accumulators; roughly 15-20 MFLOP/step on top of the encoder/decoder. Memory +768+3 floats. One-off transition table build: O(#train transitions) over a window of 5, minutes on CPU, done once before epoch 0.
ideas.coupling_equation: kappa_{l,k} = (kappa_max/sqrt(e)) * clip( rho_{l,k}^{-1}, e^{-1/2}, e^{1/2} ),  rho_{l,k} = ( (1/occ_{l,k}) * sum_{i:a_{l,i}=k} b_i/pop_i ) / ( (1/K) * sum_{k'} (1/occ_{l,k'}) * sum_{i:a_{l,i}=k'} b_i/pop_i ),  D_{l,k}(r) = kappa_{l,k}^{-1/2} * acosh( 1 + 2*kappa_{l,k}*||x_l - c_{l,k}||^2 / ((1-kappa_{l,k}||x_l||^2)(1-kappa_{l,k}||c_{l,k}||^2)) ),  x_l = exp_0(z_l), z_l = (c*/s_l)*r_l, c_{l,k} = exp_0(e_{l,k}).
ideas.coupling_path: One pathway: train-split transitions -> b_i/pop_i -> per-codeword reach-per-occupant phi_{l,k} (with occupancy in the denominator) -> rho_{l,k} -> curvature kappa_{l,k} -> geodesic distance D_{l,k} -> argmin assignment k*, commitment loss gradient and codebook pull -> encoder and codeword positions next step. Removing behaviour sets rho=1 and loses the per-codeword curvature structure (all codewords identical curvature); removing curvature removes the metric in which rho is expressed, so the behaviour term no longer inflates any distance. Neither can be deleted without changing k*, the gradients and therefore the SIDs.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If equality of level capacity comes from residual renormalisation and anti-hoarding comes from the per-codeword curvature field, then level 1 keeps its GEOCAP-level separation (valid_l1_hard_er well below the 16.390 baseline, positive_hit_rate near 0.12) while level 3 spreads (l3_collision below 0.35, level-3 assignment entropy and distinct triples up), and Stage 3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065; the mechanism is worth keeping if the single full run shows both the non-regressed level-1 numbers and the level-3 spread together, since either alone was already seen without a recall gain.

e the RQ quantiser, at every level: the residual is exp-mapped, the codeword is exp-mapped in the same chart, the assignment argmin uses the curvature-scaled geodesic distance, the decode uses log_0 of that same codeword point, and the commitment/codebook terms are the squared geodesic distances; curvature acts on assignment, on the codebook parameter update and on the encoder gradient.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare ball of measured per-(level,codeword) negative curvature kappa_{l,k} in [kappa_max/e, kappa_max] with kappa_max = 0.9/tanh^2(0.9) = 1.754 (unit-ball coordinates, curvature -kappa_{l,k}), used through exp_0, log_0 and the curvature-scaled geodesic distance acosh(1 + 2k||x-c||^2/((1-k||x||^2)(1-k||c||^2)))/sqrt(k).
ideas.key_change: Each level's residual is renormalised by its own measured RMS to a fixed shell of the unit Poincare ball (giving level 3 the same capacity as level 1), and each codeword k at level l is scored with the Poincare distance of curvature -kappa_{l,k}, where kappa_{l,k} is raised when the codeword's behavioural reach per occupant falls below its level mean, which inflates that codeword's distances and makes the hoarding codewords shed items at every level, deepest included.
ideas.leakage_boundary: C, pop and b are built exclusively from Stage-2 training-split interactions before the first epoch and are frozen; the codeword statistics occ and phi are accumulators over training batches only; no validation or test item ever contributes a transition, an occupancy or a curvature value, and SID construction therefore cannot see held-out interactions. The curvature field is a within-training measured control variable, and the Stage-3 protocol sees only the frozen SIDs.
ideas.motivation: The previous capacity-cell mechanism (GEOCAP-RQ) won at level 1 (valid_l1_hard_er 3.885 vs 16.390, positive_hit_rate 0.1222 vs 0.0794) but its cell sizes were driven by item popularity, so at level 3 a few high-demand codewords absorbed most items (l3_collision 0.549 > 0.35 gate) and Stage 3 never ran. The real problem is that the quantity that decides how much room a codeword gets must respond to that level's residual occupancy and to behaviour, not to item popularity: a codeword should only be allowed to keep a large cell if the items it holds actually carry behavioural reach beyond their share.
ideas.novelty: The curvature is not a global constant, not a per-item radius and not a transport between charts: it is a per-(level,codeword) NEGATIVE CURVATURE FIELD produced by a closed-loop, occupancy-normalised behavioural statistic (behavioural reach per occupant divided by the level mean), and every codeword is scored with its own curvature inside one shared coordinate chart (x = exp_0(z), c = exp_0(e), same tangent system, nothing is moved to another chart). The curvature enters assignment, the commitment gradient and the codebook pull simultaneously, and it is detached (a measured control variable), so behaviour shapes the geometry rather than being added as a side loss. It differs from GEOCAP (popularity-sized radii, one curvature), from BRad-RQ (behaviour-scaled radius) and from the rejected holonomy arm (cross-chart transport).
ideas.observables: (a) per-level assignment entropy and level-3 distinct prefixes / l3_collision (expect l3_collision far below 0.549 and below 0.35, distinct prefixes up from 4236); (b) the number of codewords whose kappa sits at the upper bound (the shedding set) and their occupancy over epochs; (c) level-1 diagnostics must stay at GEOCAP order (valid_l1_hard_er near 3.9, positive_hit_rate near 0.12), not baseline order; (d) gradient norm of the encoder through the geodesic commitment term should differ in sign structure per level (measured), and prefix behaviour predictability (given prefix, entropy of the next code) should fall; (e) the judgement: Stage3 test_recall@10 > 0.065 vs baseline 0.0555.
risks: Detached EMA curvature lags assignment drift and can oscillate (mitigated by the narrow bounded range and the epoch-horizon EMA); cross-curvature comparison is scale-biased so high-kappa codewords can be starved permanently (bounded by kappa_max and by log-clipping rho); s_l for level 3 may be tiny, so renormalisation amplifies noise and saturates the clamp (numeric floor s_l >= 0.01*s_1); sparse items (pop=1) make b_i/pop_i noisy; acosh argument can overflow or fall below 1; the extra curvature term in the commitment loss could dominate the reconstruction term if the frozen coefficient is large.
ideas.safeguards: clamp ||z||<=0.9 and ||e||<=0.9 before exp_0 so kappa_max*tanh^2(0.9)=0.9 leaves a >=0.10 denominator margin; clamp both ball denominators to >=0.05; acosh argument floored at 1+1e-6 and capped at 1e6; safe norms sqrt(||.||^2+1e-8) to avoid 0/0 at the origin; s_l floored at 0.01*s_1 and capped at 10*s_1; pop_i floored at 1; occ floored at eps=1e-6 with empty codewords set to rho=1; kappa computed with detach() and clip so no gradient flows through a measured statistic and no rho can explode; kappa hard-bounded in [0.6453,1.754] so no distance can diverge; behaviour table built from the train split only and frozen before epoch 0; straight-through x_q = x + (x_q - x).detach() is never replaced, so encoder gradients never vanish through the quantiser; assignment and reconstruction read the same e_{l,k} parameter (distance point c=exp_0(e), decode log_0(c)=e), so the codebook cannot be optimised to two different positions.
ideas.spec_equations:
# once, before epoch 0 (train split only)
pop_i = count of i in train; C_ij = window-5 directed co-occurrence counts
b_i = sum_j C_ij / sqrt(max(pop_i,1)*max(pop_j,1))
# per step, detached state
for l in 1..3:
    s_l <- (1-m)*s_l + m*sqrt(mean_i ||r_{l,i}||^2),  m = 1/24, init from batch 1, s_l >= 0.01*s_1
    z_{l,i} = (0.9/s_l)*r_{l,i}; z <- z*min(1, 0.9/||z||)
    x_{l,i} = tanh(||z||)*z/||z||

# exp_0
    e_{l,k} <- e_{l,k}*min(1, 0.9/||e_{l,k}||); c = tanh(||e||)*e/||e||   # exp_0
    # curvature field (detached, from previous step's accumulators)
    phi_{l,k} = (1/max(occ_{l,k},eps)) * sum_{i:a=k} b_i/max(pop_i,1)
    rho_{l,k} = phi_{l,k} / mean_k'(phi_{l,k'})
    kappa_{l,k} = (1.754/sqrt(e)) * clip(rho_{l,k}^{-1}, e^{-1/2}, e^{1/2})
    u2 = ||x - c||^2; ax = clamp(1-kappa*||x||^2, 0.05, 1); ac = clamp(1-kappa*||c||^2, 0.05, 1)
    D_{l,k} = (1/sqrt(kappa)) * acosh(max(1 + 2*kappa*u2/(ax*ac), 1+1e-6))
    k*_l = argmin_k D_{l,k}
    q_l = (s_l/0.9) * log_0(c_{l,k*_l}) = (s_l/0.9) * e_{l,k*}      # same point as the distance
    r_{l+1} = r_l - q_l
    occ_{l,k} <- EMA(EMA_horizon 1 epoch) of hard counts over (l,k); a_{l,i} = k*_l
# reconstruction, STE preserved
x_q = x + (Decode(q_1+q_2+q_3) - x).detach()
L = L_rec(x, x_q) + L_code + beta_frozen * sum_l D_{l,k*_l}(r_l)^2
L_code = sum_l [ D_{l,k*}(sg(r_l))^2 pull on c_{l,k*} + D_{l,k*}(sg(c_{l,k*}))^2 encoder commitment ]
# switches: BEHAV_OFF -> b_i/pop_i := 1 ; GEOM_OFF -> exp/log := identity, D := ||z-e||*rho^{-1/2}
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Input: per level the residual r_l (B x 32), codeword tangent table e_l (256 x 32), detached state {s_l, occ_l (256), phi_l (256)}, static behaviour table {b_i, pop_i} (24556), and switches (BEHAV_OFF, GEOM_OFF). Output: k*_l (B int), q_l (B x 32) as the same-chart decode of the assigned codeword, D_{l,k*} (B), the curvature vector kappa_l (256), the updated detached state, and the per-level prefix codes used to build SIDs. Pure function of its inputs at each step; the only cross-step state is the EMA state.

ideas.title: Behaviour reach per occupant becomes each codeword's own negative curvature, on a residual-renormalised Poincare chart, so deep-level codes spread instead of collapsing.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: PRIOR_MODE = uniform: the prior term is replaced by log 1 = 0 (equivalently B_l ≡ 0), so logit = −d_H only; β_l, τ_l, the curved residual, the Möbius subtraction and the straight-through soft assignment are all unchanged. The switch exists in the code and is exercised by a unit check that the prior term is exactly zero, but this arm is never trained.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The default and only trained configuration: PRIOR_MODE = behaviour and GEOM_MODE = poincare simultaneously, i.e. curved assignment, curved residual, curved decode and the pair transition prior in one logit. One run, 3000 Stage-2 epochs on four cards, frozen Stage-3 protocol, no early stopping, no sweep, no second seed.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: GEOM_MODE = euclidean: d_H becomes ||p−q||, and exp_0 / log_0 / ⊖ become the identity (β_l·U_{l,k} and plain r_{l−1} − β_l·U_{l,k}), so the label is the same residual-scaled Euclidean residual quantiser; the behaviour prior is retained with the Euclidean cost. The switch exists in the code and is checked by asserting that no arcosh/tanh/artanh is on the forward path, but this arm is never trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the Stage-2 training split only (the same training user sequences with adjacent timestamps used to form the training items): form the directed multiset of consecutive pairs (i_t → i_{t+1}) with gap 1 inside each user sequence; add the Stage-1 co-consumption pairs only if the baseline already uses them for training items, otherwise not. Once per epoch, run one no-grad forward pass over the 24556 training items' encoder outputs with the current codebook, cache T_l(i) = argmax code at level l, and accumulate B_l[k',k] += 1 for every training pair with T_{l−1}(i)=k' and T_l(j)=k (k'=0 dummy at l=1). The table is frozen for the whole following epoch, is integer-valued, and never carries gradient.
ideas.behavior_signal: Per-pair directed successor-code transition counts: for each level l, the count of training-split sequences in which an item i with level-(l−1) code k' is immediately followed by an item j whose level-l code is k. The signal is the code-level successor distribution B_l[k',·], used as a row-normalised prior over level-l codes; it is not item popularity, and it is not the item's own context entropy.
ideas.cost_estimate: Relative to the baseline RQ-VAE Stage 2, ≈1.02× per step plus ≈4% per epoch. At the frozen scale, 24556 training items over 24 steps/epoch gives ≈1023 items per step; the per-level cost matrix is 1023×256 geodesic distances (3 levels, d=64 ⇒ ≈50 MFLOP of matmul-equivalent work, the same order as the baseline Euclidean assignment it replaces), and the added hyperbolic elementwise work (tanh, 2·artanh, arcosh, Möbius subtraction) touches only 1023×64 and 256×64 arrays, well under 2% of the step. The prior step is three row gathers plus a log — negligible. The only real addition is the epoch-boundary refresh: one no-grad encoder forward over 24556 items (≈24 steps' worth) plus a sparse scatter-add, ≈+4.2% per epoch. Total Stage 2 wall clock ≈+5–8%; Stage 3 protocol, epochs and card count unchanged. Extra parameters: zero (U has the baseline codebook shape). Extra buffers: three K×K int32 tables and three K×K float priors (≈0.25 MB and 0.75 MB), plus 2L scalars.
ideas.coupling_equation: logit_{i,k}^{(l)} = −d_H( exp_0(r_{l−1,i}/β_l), exp_0(U_{l,k}) ) − (1/ln K)·log( K·(B_l[k'_i,k] + 1)/(S_l[k'_i] + K) ), with d_H the arcosh Poincaré distance of curvature −1, B_l[k'_i,·] the training-only successor-code transition counts conditioned on the item's own level-(l−1) code, and β_l the measured residual RMS of level l; the code exponentiated is exactly the code decoded: β_l·log_0(q_{l,k}) = β_l·U_{l,k}.
ideas.coupling_path: One pathway, no parallel branch: r_{l−1} → normalise by measured β_l → exp_0 into the ball → geodesic distance to exp_0(U_{l,k}) → combined in a single logit with the pair prior log π_{k'_i}[k], where k'_i is the item's own level-(l−1) code and π is the row-normalised training transition count → straight-through softmax → argmax code k_l → (a) decodes through the same log_0 position into the STE reconstruction, and (b) produces the next residual by Möbius subtraction in the same ball. Removing the prior changes the logit (behaviour-off) and removing the curvature changes the distance, the decode and the residual (geometry-off), so neither term is a decoration.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: The idea is worth keeping only if: (i) the first-order gain survives — valid_l1_hard_er ≤ 6 and valid_l1_positive_hit_rate ≥ 0.11, i.e. no return to the baseline order of magnitude (16.390 / 0.0794); (ii) the third level spreads — l3_collision < 0.25, i.e. clears the 35% Stage-3 gate that GEOCAP's 0.549 broke, with level-3 effective code count (perplexity of the l3 code histogram over training items) materially above 256·exp(−0.549·ln?) ≈ the GEOCAP collapse level and with level2_distinct_prefixes ≥ 4000; (iii) the behaviour prior is predictable rather than noise — the l3 code actually chosen lies in the top-5 of its own prior row π_{k'} at a rate above the 5/256 uniform baseline, measured on training item pairs only as a diagnostic; (iv) the single frozen Stage-3 run reports test_recall@10 > 0.065 (baseline 0.0555, historical best 0.0638). Any one of (i)–(iii) failing means the coupling is decorative even if recall moves.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In quantisation, at every level of the residual-quantiser chain: the residual and the code tangents are exponentiated into the ball and compared by the geodesic distance in the assignment cost; the same exp_0/log_0 pair defines the decoded code vector for the straight-through reconstruction; and the residual passed to the next level is produced by Möbius subtraction inside that same ball. It also sets the cell size, because the tangent-space normalisation is β_l, the measured residual RMS of that level.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature c = −1 in the Poincaré ball: geodesic distance d_H(p,q) = arcosh(1 + 2||p−q||²/((1−||p||²)(1−||q||²))), exponential map at the origin exp_0(v) = tanh(||v||/2)·v/(||v||+1e-8), logarithmic map log_0(p) = 2·artanh(||p||)·p/(||p||+1e-8), and Möbius subtraction a ⊖ b = a ⊕ (−b) with a ⊕ b = ((1+2a·b+||b||²)a + (1−||a||²)b)/(1+2a·b+||a||²||b||²). Curvature is fixed, not trainable; no constant is chosen by search.
ideas.key_change: The assignment logit at level l is the Poincaré geodesic distance between the residual and the code, both exponentiated into the same ball after dividing by the layer's measured residual scale β_l, minus a 1/lnK-scaled log of the row-normalised pair transition prior between the item's level-(l−1) code and the candidate level-l code. Codes are selected by a straight-through softmax whose temperature is the measured median top1–top2 cost margin, and the residual is re-projected with Möbius subtraction inside the same chart.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition counts use only interactions from the training split, over the 24556 training items, and only the previous epoch's cached argmax codes of those training items. Validation and test interactions never enter B_l, never enter β_l or τ_l (which are minibatch training statistics), and never enter the codebook or the SID assignment. No Stage-3 label, no test sequence and no validation split item is read during SID construction; Stage 3 consumes the frozen SIDs and interacts with nothing in this mechanism.
ideas.motivation: This is a curvature mechanism, and it repairs the second-order collapse that GEOCAP-RQ showed. GEOCAP's first-order gain was real (valid_l1_hard_er 3.885 vs baseline 16.390; valid_l1_positive_hit_rate 0.1222 vs 0.0794; level2_distinct_prefixes 4236; l3_refinement_gain_bits 2.82), but its third level degenerated (l3_collision 0.549 against the 35% Stage-3 gate), so no recall was measured. The cause is structural: GEOCAP made each codeword's cell size and a per-codeword additive distance offset grow with that item's *own* demand, so a few high-demand cells absorbed the residual mass at level 3. RSPC-RQ changes both quantities: the cell size becomes the layer's measured residual scale (a residual/occupancy statistic), and the behaviour term becomes a row-normalised, pair-conditioned log-likelihood ratio whose mean log-weight inside every context row is 0 unless that row carries real transition information, so it can tilt which code an item takes inside its context but can never globally inflate demand for a codeword. A straight-through soft assignment with a measured temperature keeps deep codewords receiving gradient instead of starving, which is the concrete mechanism that makes level 3 spread.
ideas.novelty: Different from the three earlier rounds. It is not GEOCAP (no per-codeword demand-derived area-law radius, no per-codeword additive offset; no popularity term anywhere). It is not holonomy-path-behaviour-rq (there is no transport of the residual into a second chart: exponentiate, subtract and decode all happen at the origin of one Poincaré ball with curvature −1, and log_0 is the exact inverse of exp_0). It is not BRad-RQ (the behaviour signal is not a per-item context entropy used to rank radii; it is a sparse per-pair transition count matrix between the item's own level-(l−1) code and its successors' level-l code). It is also not a Euclidean quantiser with a behaviour suffix: the geodesic distance is the term that separates items inside a context row, the curved subtraction defines the residual that the next level sees, and the temperature is measured from the geodesic cost margin.
ideas.observables: (1) SID assignment: valid_l1_hard_er stays ≤ 6 and valid_l1_positive_hit_rate ≥ 0.11 (no return to the baseline 16.390 / 0.0794 order of magnitude); level2_distinct_prefixes ≥ 4000. (2) Third-level dispersion: l3_collision falls below 0.25 (from GEOCAP's 0.549) and the perplexity of the level-3 code histogram over training items rises materially, so the Stage-3 35% gate passes. (3) Parameter update: the codebook gradient is spread over more than one code per item at level 3 (nonzero mass in the softmax above the argmax), and the level-3 codebook rows all receive nonzero accumulated gradient. (4) Prefix behaviour predictability: the chosen level-3 code is in the top-5 of its own prior row π_{k'} at a rate above the uniform 5/256 baseline. (5) Stage 3: test_recall@10 > 0.065 on the single frozen run.
risks: At l=1 the prior row is the single dummy row 0, so the prior degenerates into a global successor-code distribution — a bounded (row-normalised to mean 1) popularity tilt. If it is strong enough to bias the l1 partition, the GEOCAP-style demand bias can partially return; the row normalisation bounds but does not eliminate this.; A self-confirming loop: B_l is built from the previous epoch's argmax assignments, so early bad prefixes can be reinforced for several epochs. The mitigation is that the conditioning code k'_i is the item's own level-(l−1) code, which moves with the encoder, and that the prior is only a bounded tilt against a geodesic term that is O(1); if the encoder is slow to move, prefixed lock-in is still possible.; Poincaré numerics: as ||p|| → 1 with clamped ||U|| ≤ 6 the conformal factor (1−||q||²) becomes small (≈0.01) and arcosh arguments can overflow or become NaN, especially with small β_l (large residuals).; The measured temperature τ_l could collapse (near-zero margin) and saturate the softmax to one-hot, or blow up and make every assignment uniform, which would destroy the residual chain; the EMA of a median is robust but not guaranteed to stay in a useful range.; The prior strength 1/ln K is derived, not tuned: if it is far too weak the run reduces to a pure curved residual quantiser and the behaviour side contributes nothing observable; that outcome cannot be repaired without a sweep, which the policy forbids.; Soft straight-through assignment changes the codebook gradient relative to hard RQ, so the comparison to the historical best 0.0638 is not perfectly like-for-like; a single run also cannot separate the coupling gain from seed noise.
ideas.safeguards: (1) STE is mandatory and explicit: x_q = x + (x_q − x).detach() on the decode path, and the softmax supplies gradient only through h = ĥ − s.detach() + s; the encoder is never fed a constant target. (2) Assignment and decode share the same code position β_l·log_0(q_{l,k}) = β_l·U_{l,k}: one chart, one set of positions, so the codebook cannot be optimised to a different location than the one it is scored against (the failure of the holonomy arm). (3) Norm clamps: ||V|| ≤ 6 so ||q|| ≤ tanh(3) ≈ 0.995; p_i rescaled to ||p|| ≤ 1 − 1e-5; both conformal factors floored at 1e-3; arcosh argument floored at 1 + 1e-8; ||p−q|| floored at 0. (4) Möbius subtraction denominator floored at 1e-8, with an automatic fallback to plain Euclidean subtraction for that step if the floor is hit, so a NaN cannot propagate into the residual chain. (5) β_l floor 1e-3 and initialisation from the first minibatch rather than zero; no division by an untrained statistic. (6) τ_l EMA floored at 1e-3 and initialised from the first minibatch margin. (7) Prior is row-normalised with Laplace smoothing, so a context row with no training transitions becomes exactly uniform (log π = 0) and no code can be favoured by absence of data; all counts are integers, refreshed only from training pairs and only from detached previous-epoch assignments. (8) The three switches PRIOR_MODE ∈ {behaviour, uniform} and GEOM_MODE ∈ {poincare, euclidean} exist as explicit code paths defaulting to [behaviour, poincare]; a shape-and-finiteness assertion runs before the first optimiser step; no arm is trained with either switch off, and no constant is swept.
ideas.spec_equations: Inputs: encoder output z ∈ R^d (baseline width), r_0 = z. Buffers: β ∈ R_+^L (EMA of per-level residual RMS, μ = 0.01, floor 1e-3), τ ∈ R_+^L (EMA of per-level median top1−top2 cost margin, floor 1e-3), B_l ∈ Z^{(K^{l−1} or K)×K} (l=1: 1×K; l≥2: K×K), S_l = B_l·1. Constants (all derived, none tuned): curvature c = −1; codebook size K (baseline, 256); prior scale 1/ln K; Laplace smoothing α = 1; EMA rate μ = 0.01; clamps listed under safeguards. Per level l = 1..L:   β_l ← (1−μ)·β_l + μ·sqrt(mean_batch ||r_{l−1}||²)   u_i ← r_{l−1,i}/β_l ;  p_i ← tanh(||u_i||/2)·u_i/(||u_i||+1e-8)   V_{l,k} ← clamp(U_{l,k}, ||·|| ≤ 6) ;  q_{l,k} ← tanh(||V_{l,k}||/2)·V_{l,k}/(||V_{l,k}||+1e-8)   D_{i,k} ← arcosh( max(1 + 2||p_i−q_{l,k}||²/((1−||p_i||²)(1−||q_{l,k}||²)), 1+1e-8) )   k'_i ← (l == 1 ? 0 : argmax_{k} s_{i,k} from level l−1)   π_{k'} ← (B_l[k',:] + 1)/(S_l[k'] + K)·K ;  L_{i,k} ← −D_{i,k} − (1/ln K)·log π_{k'_i}[k]   m_i ← median_k_of(L_{i,(1)} − L_{i,(2)})  (two smallest costs, per minibatch)   τ_l ← (1−μ)·τ_l + μ·m_i   s_{i,·} ← softmax(L_{i,·}/τ_l) ;  ĥ_{i,k} ← 1[k = argmax s_{i,k}]   h_i ← ĥ_i − s_i.detach() + s_i   x_q ← x + (Σ_l β_l·log_0(q_{l,argmax}) − x).detach()          # explicit STE, preserved   r_{l,i} ← β_l·log_0( p_i ⊖ q_{l,argmax} )                     # same chart Loss: L_recon(x, x_q) + baseline commit/entropy terms, unchanged. Epoch boundary: one no-grad forward over 24556 training items → T_l(i) = argmax s; rebuild B_l from training pairs (i_t → i_{t+1}). Outputs: prefix tuple (k_1,k_2,k_3) per item, x_q, and the level-wise code histograms.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Takes: the encoder output z ∈ R^d of a training item (plus β, τ and B_l buffers), the learnable code tangents U ∈ R^{L×K×d}, and the training-split directed pairs (i_t → i_{t+1}) at epoch boundaries. Returns: per level l the straight-through soft assignment s_i ∈ Δ^{K−1} and hard code k_l ∈ {1..K}; the reconstructed vector x_q = x + (Σ_l β_l U_{l,argmax} − x).detach() ∈ R^d; the next residual r_l ∈ R^d; and, at epoch boundaries, the refreshed integer tables B_l. The SID handed to the generative recommender is (k_1,k_2,k_3).

specification.text: Parameters and buffers (d = encoder output width, K = 256 codes per level, L = 3 levels): learnable code tangents U ∈ R^{L×K×d} (exactly the baseline codebook shape, initialised from the baseline Euclidean codebook); non-trainable buffers β_1..β_L ∈ R_+ (EMA of the per-level residual RMS, detached); τ_1..τ_L ∈ R_+ (EMA of the measured median top1–top2 geodesic cost margin, detached); B_1 ∈ Z^{1×K}, B_2, B_3 ∈ Z^{K×K} (training-split directed transition counts, refreshed once per epoch, detached, no gradient). Per level l = 1..L, on a minibatch of residuals r_{l−1}: (1) β_l ← (1−μ)β_l + μ·RMS(r_{l−1}) with μ = 0.01 and floor 1e-3 (detached); buffer initialised on the first minibatch, not at zero. (2) u_i = r_{l−1,i}/β_l; p_i = tanh(||u_i||/2)·u_i/(||u_i||+1e-8); q_{l,k} = tanh(||U_{l,k}||/2)·U_{l,k}/(||U_{l,k}||+1e-8), with ||U_{l,k}|| clamped to ≤ 6. (3) d_H(i,k) = arcosh(1 + 2||p_i − q_{l,k}||²/((1−||p_i||²)(1−||q_{l,k}||²))). (4) k'_i = the level-(l−1) code already chosen for item i in this forward pass (k'=0 dummy for l=1); prior row π_{k'} = (B_l[k',:] + 1)/(S_l[k'] + K)·K with S_l[k'] = Σ_k B_l[k',k]. (5) logit_{i,k} = −d_H(i,k) − (1/ln K)·log π_{k'}[k]; s_{i,k} = softmax_k(logit_{i,k}/τ_l); h_i = one_hot(argmax_k s_{i,k}) − s_{i,k}.detach() + s_{i,k} (straight-through hard code, soft gradient to costs, no detach on the decode path). (6) Decode with the SAME code positions: x_q = x + (Σ_l β_l·log_0(q_{l,argmax}) − x).detach(), i.e. the explicit STE x_q = x + (x_q − x).detach() is preserved and β_l·log_0(q) = β_l·U_{l,k} is used both in the reconstruction and in the assignment (identical positions, one chart). (7) Curved residual: r_l = β_l·log_0(p_i ⊖ q_{l,argmax}). Epoch boundary only: one no-grad forward pass over the 24556 training items caches the argmax code per level, then B_l[k',k] is rebuilt from the training-split directed pairs (i_t → i_{t+1}).

ideas.title: Residual-scaled Poincaré assignment with a per-pair successor-code prior and same-chart curved residual subtraction

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: `use_branching=True` -> False sets h_{l,m} := hbar_l for every parent, so the middle factor is identically 1 and kappa_hat^{beh-off}_{l,m} = clip((S_{l,m}/S_l)^{1/2}((n_{l,m}+1)/(nbar_l+1))^{1/2}, 0.25, 4); the geodesic machinery is unchanged. This arm exists in the code and is never trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: `curvature_mode='poincare'` and `use_branching=True`: kappa_hat_{l,m} = clip((S_{l,m}/S_l)^{1/2} ((h_{l,m}+eps_h)/(hbar_l+eps_h))^{1/2} ((n_{l,m}+1)/(nbar_l+1))^{1/2}, 0.25, 4) with the geodesic argmin and the geodesic commitment term. This is the single official run of the round, trained once on the frozen 3000-epoch Stage-2 budget and the frozen Stage-3 protocol.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: `curvature_mode='euclidean'` forces kappa_hat := 1e-6 for every (l,m), so rad_c(v)=v, ctilde/z-tilde are the plain scaled vectors, the arcosh branch is replaced by delta = 2||u - E_l[k]/sqrt(S_l)||, and the commitment term is the ordinary squared Euclidean distance: the same code, the same STE, the same statistics, only flat. This arm exists in the code and is never trained in this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training split only: for every training user sequence and every consecutive pair (v_t, v_{t+1}) with v_t != v_{t+1}, increment N[v_t, v_{t+1}] once per user (deduplicated per user so heavy users do not dominate); sparse CSR over the 24556 training items. From the current (detached) assignment snapshot, residents I_{l,m} = items whose level-(l-1) code is m; successor mass s_{m,j} = sum_{i in I} N[i,j]; p_{m,j} = s_{m,j}/sum_j s_{m,j}; aggregate successors into level-1 prefix classes c: q_{m,c} = sum_{j: l1code(j)=c} p_{m,j}; h_{l,m} = H(q)/log K_1 in [0,1]; hbar_l = mean over occupied parents; n_{l,m} = |I_{l,m}|. All three are EMAs updated inside the normal training batches (the sample already yields both the item's code and its next item, so no extra pass).
ideas.behavior_signal: Per-parent-code successor branching entropy of the directed item-transition graph (a behaviour-conditioned per-code measure of how diversely the residents of a parent semantic cell are consumed next), together with the parent's occupancy.
ideas.cost_estimate: One extra BxK geodesic distance per level (B=1024, K_l=256, d=32), implemented in the Lorentz model as one BxK GEMM per level, so about +3% to +8% step time and no extra forward pass for any statistic (all EMAs are accumulated from the batches already being trained). At the frozen scale (24556 training items, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs = 72k steps) that is roughly +0.1 to +0.3 GPU-hour per card, memory +O(B*K) per level for the distance matrix (about 1 MB per level at B=1024, K=256 in fp32). No change to the number of epochs, no early stopping.
ideas.coupling_equation: kappa_hat_{l,m} = clip( (S_{l,m}/S_l)^{1/2} * ((h_{l,m}+eps_h)/(hbar_l+eps_h))^{1/2} * ((n_{l,m}+1)/(nbar_l+1))^{1/2}, 1/4, 4 ), and k_i^{(l)} = argmin_k arcosh( 1 + 2 kappa_hat_{l,m} || ztilde_i (-)_{kappa_hat} ctilde_{l,k} ||^2 / ((1 - kappa_hat |ztilde_i|^2)(1 - kappa_hat |ctilde_{l,k}|^2)) ) with ztilde_i = Exp_0^{kappa_hat}( r_i^{(l)} / sqrt(S_l) ), ctilde_{l,k} = Exp_0^{kappa_hat}( E_l[k] / sqrt(S_l) ). Here h_{l,m}/hbar_l is the behaviour term and kappa_hat is the curved term; the behaviour term acts only through the curvature of the geodesic distance, and the geodesic distance acts only through the behaviour-conditioned curvature.
ideas.coupling_path:
training-only successor-branching entropy h_{l,m} -> kappa_hat_{l,m} -> curvature of the ball in which the level-l residual and the level-l codeword are both exp-mapped -> geodesic argmin that emits code k_i and geodesic commitment gradient -> codebook/encoder update -> next epoch's parent occupancy and residual statistics. Switch the behaviour factor off and kappa_hat loses its dependence on h; switch curvature off and the same pathway becomes the Euclidean nearest-neighbour + squared-error commitment. Either change alters k_i, the gradient on E_l and hence the emitted SIDs, so the coupling is the core com

putation and not an add-on.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If curvature conditioned on the parent's own residual/occupancy/branching is the right second-order fix, then at level 3 the curvature field is non-degenerate (IQR of kappa_hat_{3,m} over occupied parents > 1.5x) and the crowded/rich parents get kappa_hat close to 4, their level-3 assignment becomes direction-dominated and spreads over materially more distinct codewords, so l3_collision falls below the 0.35 Stage-3 gate while level-1 separation does not regress to baseline (valid_l1_hard_er stays below ~8, valid_l1_positive_hit_rate >= 0.11), and Stage3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065 (baseline 0.0555, prior best 0.0638). It is falsified in one run if l3_collision stays >= 0.35, or level-1 hard ER returns to ~16, or test_R@10 <= 0.065.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ quantisation of Stage-2 training at every one of the three levels - both in the assignment (geodesic argmin used to emit the semantic-ID digit) and in the commitment term that produces the gradient on the codebook and (through the assignment) on the encoder. It is not in the decoder and it is not a separate auxiliary loss.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball exponential map at the origin, rad_c(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)||v||) v/(sqrt(c)||v||), with curvature -c, c = kappa_hat in [0.25,4] measured per (level, parent cell) in level-RMS units, plus the Mobius difference and the arcosh geodesic distance in the same ball of curvature c (optionally evaluated in the equivalent Lorentz model, d = arcosh(-c <z,c>_L)/sqrt(c), which is the same number).
ideas.key_change:
Each level's residual is normalised by the measured level RMS and quantised in a Poincare ball of curvature kappa_hat_{l,m} in [0.25,4], where m is

the item's parent codeword at level l-1 and kappa_hat is the clipped geometric mean of three measured ratios (residual energy of that parent, successor-branching entropy of that parent, occupancy of that parent); the code index is the geodesic argmin and the commitment term is the squared geodesic distance, while the straight-through reconstruction path is byte-identical to the baseline.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Transitions, occupancies and branching entropies are built exclusively from training-split sequences and from item embeddings learned on the training split; the assignment snapshot is computed on training items only. No validation or test interaction is ever read while constructing the codes, so a validation/test item's identity, popularity or neighbours cannot influence its own or any other item's SID; the validation set is used only for the recorded diagnostics and the test set only for the final Stage-3 recall.
ideas.motivation: GEOCAP-RQ fixed level-1 separation but collapsed level 3 (l3_collision 0.549 > 0.35) because the size of a capacity cell was a function of the item's own demand/popularity, so a few crowded high-demand cells swallowed the deep codewords and the level-3 residual was never split. What is needed is a geometric quantity that decides how finely a deep cell is cut from the residual that is actually still unquantized inside that cell, and from how diversely its residents behave - not from how popular they are.
ideas.novelty: Not an additive per-codeword radial offset on a fixed metric (GEOCAP), not a two-leg parallel transport between charts (holonomy arm), not a standalone hyperbolic auxiliary loss. Curvature itself is the conditioning variable: a measured (not trained) scalar kappa_hat per (level, parent cell) drives the Poincare exponential map of BOTH the residual and the codeword of that level, so the same codeword sits at a different hyperbolic radius depending on which parent cell the item came from, and the residual/codeword comparison becomes direction-dominated exactly where that parent's level-l residual is rich, branchy and crowded. Level 1 is provably run at unit curvature in level-RMS units, so the mechanism has no free curvature constant to tune.
ideas.observables: (a) the distribution of kappa_hat_{3,m} over occupied parent cells (report median, IQR, mass at the clip bounds) - it must vary, otherwise the coupling is inert; (b) rounded l3_collision must fall below 0.35 (GEOCAP 0.549) while level-2 distinct prefixes stay near or above 4236 and l3_refinement_gain_bits stays near or above 2.82; (c) valid_l1_hard_er must stay far below the baseline 16.390 and valid_l1_positive_hit_rate at or above 0.11 so the first-order separation is not lost; (d) usage entropy and the number of used codewords per level; (e) Stage-3 test_recall@10 must exceed 0.065 versus baseline 0.0555 and prior best 0.0638. All diagnostics are recorded, and only (e) is the judgement.
risks:
["Level 1 is also curved (kappa_hat=1 by construction), so the first-order separation that GEOCAP reached through radial offsets may not be reproduced and l1_hard_er may drift back toward the baseline 16.39.", "The curved commitment term scales gradients by d(delta^2)/dE, which grows near the ball boundary; without the standardisation safeguard it can destabilise the codebook early in training.", "The EMA statistics of S_{l,m}, n_{l,m} and h_{l,m} lag the codebook, so kappa_hat can oscillate between epochs and make deep assignments flip.", "Successor branching entropy is a coarse proxy

for residual diversity; if branchy parents are not the residual-rich ones the behaviour factor adds noise instead of sharpening level 3.", "If the level-3 residual is genuinely low-dimensional, no curvature can spread the collisions and the collision gate fails for a reason the mechanism cannot address.", "Early in training S_l is still tiny, so the Euclidean degeneracy branch and the clip lower bound may dominate for the first few hundred epochs and lock the deep levels into one geometry."]
ideas.safeguards: clamp the arcosh argument to >= 1+1e-7 and the output to 1e4; clamp the codebook loss per element (gradient clip 1.0) and standardise delta^2 by its detached batch median before weighting so the curved term has the same scale as the Euclidean one at every epoch; use max(||v||,1e-8) in rad_c and branch to the identity when kappa_hat < 1e-6 (Euclidean limit) so no 0/0 appears; recompute (1 - c|z|^2) with float64-free but clamped arguments at >= 1e-6, since |rad_c(v)| < 1/sqrt(c) strictly; require |ztilde| <= (1-1e-6)/sqrt(kappa_hat) after the map and rescale if violated; EMPTY cells (n_{l,m}=0) inherit kappa_hat = 1 instead of dividing; Laplace smoothing 1e-3 on h; bias-corrected EMAs and a detached copy of all statistics so no gradient flows through the curvature; drop the h factor at the very first epoch (hbar_l undefined) and use kappa_hat=1 there; gradient-norm watchdog that falls back to Euclidean only if a NaN/Inf appears (a numeric guard, not an ablation arm).
ideas.spec_equations:
"u = r^(l) / (sqrt(S_l) + 1e-8)  # S_l = EMA of E||r^(l)||^2
kappa_hat = clip( (S_{l,m}/S_l)**0.5 * ((h_{l,m}+1e-3)/(hbar_l+1e-3))**0.5 * ((n_{l,m}+1)/(nbar_l+1))**0.5, 0.25, 4.0 )
def rad(c, v):  n = norm(v);  return v if c < 1e-6 else tanh(sqrt(c)*n)/(sqrt(c)*max(n,1e-8)) * v
zt = rad(kappa_hat, u);  ct = rad(kappa_hat, E_l / (sqrt(S_l)+1e-8))
num = 2*kappa_hat*sqnorm(mobius_sub(zt, ct, kappa_hat))
den = (1 - kappa_hat*sqnorm(zt)) * (1 - kappa_hat*sqnorm(ct))
delta = arcosh(clamp(1 + num/den, min=1+1e-7));  k_i = argmin_k delta[k]
L_commit_l = lambda_commit * delta[k_i]**2        # replaces the Euclidean commitment, same lambda_commit
r_q = E_l[k_i];  r_next = r + (r_q - r).detach()  # STE preserved verbatim
after step: EMA-update S_l, S_{l,m}, n_{l,m}, h_{l,m} with decay 0.99, bias corrected"
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs:
Inputs: encoder embeddings h_i (B x d), the three codebooks E_l (K_l x d, K_l = 256 as in the baseline), the detached

parent code m(i) from level l-1, the detached EMA statistics S_l, S_{l,m}, n_{l,m}, h_{l,m}, and the frozen training-only transition matrix N (CSR, 24556 x 24556). Outputs: the level-l code index k_i^(l) for every item (i.e. the three semantic-ID digits), the straight-through quantised residuals r_q^(l) feeding the unchanged reconstruction path, the curved commitment losses L_commit_l and their gradients on E_l and on the encoder, and the refreshed detached EMAs used by the next step.

specification.text: Stage-2 only. Levels l=1..3, codebook E_l in R^{K_l x d}, r_i^(1)=encoder(h_i). Detached bias-corrected EMA (decay 0.99) after each optimizer step: S_l = E||r_i^(l)||^2; per parent code m of level l-1: n_{l,m}, S_{l,m}=E[||r^(l)||^2 | parent=m], h_{l,m}=successor branching entropy; hbar_l, nbar_l = means over occupied parents. Per item and level: u_i = r_i^(l)/(sqrt(S_l)+1e-8); kappa_hat_{l,m} = clip( (S_{l,m}/S_l)^0.5 * ((h_{l,m}+1e-3)/(hbar_l+1e-3))^0.5 * ((n_{l,m}+1)/(nbar_l+1))^0.5, 0.25, 4 ). rad_c(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)||v||) * v / (sqrt(c)||v||) (v itself if c<1e-6); ztilde_i = rad_c(u_i); ctilde_{l,k} = rad_c(E_l[k]/(sqrt(S_l)+1e-8)); delta_ik = arcosh(1 + 2c||ztilde_i (-) ctilde_k||^2 / ((1-c|ztilde_i|^2)(1-c|ctilde_k|^2))); k_i = argmin_k delta_ik. Commitment term at level l becomes lambda_commit * delta_{i,k_i}^2 (replaces the Euclidean commitment, same lambda_commit from the baseline config). Reconstruction untouched: r_q^(l)=E_l[k_i]; r^(l+1) = r^(l) + (r_q^(l) - r^(l)).detach(); x_q = h + (sum_l r_q^(l) - h).detach() - the STE line is preserved verbatim. Parent m for level 1 is the global code 0, so n=nbar, S=S_1, h=hbar_1 and kappa_hat_{1,0}=1 exactly.

ideas.title: PARENTCURV-RQ - parent-conditioned, residual/occupancy/branching-scaled curvature field for the RQ semantic-ID quantizer

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: btilde identically 0 in the occupancy update, so N_{l,k} is a plain assignment count and rho_{l,k} depends only on geometry and occupancy; code exists and is exercised by unit checks, but no such arm is trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The single trained run: behaviour-weighted occupancy inside the hyperbolic area-law radius, the geodesic assignment, the same codeword positions for assignment and reconstruction, and the unchanged straight-through estimator x_q = z + (x_q - z).detach().
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: c_l -> 0 in the same equation: cost becomes Euclidean ||r/s_l - T_{l,k}|| / rho^E_{l,k} with the Euclidean volume law rho^E_{l,k} = R_ref^E * p_{l,k}^{1/d} and R_ref^E = s_l, so the same behaviour-weighted occupancy drives the same kind of radius with no curvature; code exists, not trained.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the Stage-2 TRAIN split only: scan each training sequence with a forward window of 3 and count directed transitions (i -> j), giving a sparse row-normalised matrix Q (24556 x 24556, one sparse pass, done once before training, frozen into a buffer). H_i = -sum_j Q_ij log Q_ij, normalised so mean(H) = 1 over warm items, btilde_i = clip(H_i/mean(H) - 1, -1, 3); items with fewer than 5 outgoing training transitions get btilde_i = 0. btilde is a frozen 24556-vector read by the epoch-level occupancy update N_{l,k} = sum over train items assigned to (l,k) of clip(1+btilde_i, 0.05, 4).
ideas.behavior_signal: Training-only user-interest branching: the Shannon entropy H_i of item i's directed successor distribution over training sequences, used as a per-item weight that is aggregated into a per-code, per-level occupancy mass.
ideas.cost_estimate: +4 to +6 percent wall clock at the frozen scale (24556 train items, 24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs). Per step: batch about 1023 items, 3 levels, K codewords per level, width d: geodesic pair cost is about 10 flops per (item, codeword) pair, so B*K*L ~ 7.9e5 pairs ~ 8 MFLOP, cheaper than the baseline's B*K*L*d ~ 25 MFLOP Euclidean distance term; the exp_0/log_0 chart maps add B*L*d ~ 1e5 flops. The only real overhead is one extra no-grad encoder forward pass over 24556 items per epoch, about 1/24 of a training epoch (about 4 percent). Behaviour preprocessing is a single sparse pass over the train transition counts (seconds, once). Memory: +3*K*d floats for T_l, +3*K floats for N_l, 24556 floats for btilde.
ideas.coupling_equation: cost_{i,k}^{(l)} = d_P^{c_l}(exp_0^{c_l}(r_i^{(l)}/s_l), exp_0^{c_l}(T_{l,k})) / [ R_ref(c_l) * g_{c_l}( m_l / (m_l + N_{l,k}(btilde)) ) ], with N_{l,k}(btilde) = sum_{i': chat_l(i')=k} clip(1 + btilde_{i'}, 0.05, 4), m_l = (1/K) sum_k N_{l,k}, R_ref(c_l) = (1/sqrt(c_l)) artanh(0.95 sqrt(c_l)), g_c(p) = arcosh(1 + p(cosh(sqrt(c) R_ref) - 1)) / (sqrt(c) R_ref). The curved term d_P^{c_l} and the behaviour term btilde meet inside the single denominator rho_{l,k}.
ideas.coupling_path: One chain, no side terms: item training-transition entropy btilde -> per-code behaviour-weighted occupancy N_{l,k}(btilde) -> volume fraction p_{l,k} = m_l/(m_l + N_{l,k}) -> hyperbolic area-law inversion with curvature c_l -> cell radius rho_{l,k} -> denominator of the geodesic assignment cost d_P^{c_l}(v, C_k)/rho_{l,k} -> hard code chat_l -> decoded residual and codeword update. Removing btilde collapses N_{l,k} to a plain count and therefore changes p and rho and the partition; removing c_l (c -> 0) changes the same radius through the Euclidean power law and the distance through d_E, and the partition again.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the inverse-occupancy hyperbolic radius is the right capacity rule, then in the single run: (i) l3_collision drops below the 0.35 Stage-3 gate while l3_refinement_gain_bits stays >= 2.8, (ii) level-1 separation does not regress (valid_l1_hard_er stays near 4, i.e. well below the 16.39 baseline, and valid_l1_positive_hit_rate >= 0.12), and (iii) Stage3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065 (beating the 0.0555 baseline and the 0.0638 historical best). If l3_collision stays above 0.35 or l1 ER returns to baseline magnitude, the mechanism is falsified.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In the quantizer only, at every residual-quantization level l = 1,2,3: the residual is mapped into the ball with exp_0^{c_l}, the codebook lives in the ball (tangent-space parameterisation T_l -> exp_0^{c_l}(T_l)), the assignment cost is the geodesic distance divided by an area-law radius of the same curvature, and the chosen codeword is decoded back with log_0^{c_l} with the same c_l. Nothing else in the model is curved.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball model with trainable per-level curvature c_l = exp(kappa_l) in [1e-3, 8] (init c_l = 1): Riemannian distance d_P^c(u,v) = (1/sqrt(c)) * arcosh(1 + 2c||u-v||^2 / ((1-c||u||^2)(1-c||v||^2))), exponential map exp_0^c(t) = tanh(sqrt(c)||t||)/(sqrt(c)||t||) * t, logarithmic map log_0^c(p) = artanh(sqrt(c)||p||)/(sqrt(c)||p||) * p, and the hyperbolic ball-area law V_c(rho) proportional to (cosh(sqrt(c) rho) - 1)/c which is inverted to turn a volume fraction into a radius.
ideas.key_change: Each level-l codeword gets rho_{l,k} = R_ref(c_l) * g_{c_l}(m_l/(m_l+N_{l,k})) where N_{l,k} is that level's behaviour-weighted hard-assignment mass from the previous epoch; the assignment cost is the Poincare distance divided by rho_{l,k}, and the reconstructed residual is log_0 of the SAME codeword position, so STE, the chart and the codeword positions are untouched.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Q and btilde are built once, before any training, from the Stage-2 train split's sequences only. Validation and test sessions are never tokenised into the scan, the frozen buffer is never recomputed from any other split, and N_l and s_l are recomputed only from the train items' own forward passes. Therefore no validation or test interaction can influence a radius, a codeword position, a curvature, or a SID; the Stage-3 evaluation reads the finished SIDs only.
ideas.motivation: GEOCAP-RQ sized each level-l codeword cell by item popularity (demand -> bigger cell). That is the wrong sign for rate-distortion: a quantizer must shrink cells where the residual density is high. At level 1 the residual mass is spread, so GEOCAP accidentally helped (valid_l1_hard_er 3.885 vs 16.390 baseline, l1 positive hit 0.1222 vs 0.0794). At level 3 the residual mass concentrates in a few cells, GEOCAP inflates exactly those cells, and the deep code degenerates: l3_collision 0.549 broke the 35% Stage-3 gate, so Stage-3 recall was never measured. The recommender problem is therefore: keep the level-1 separation gain while making deep SID prefixes finer where the level's own residual occupancy is high, so that SID prefixes stay behaviour-discriminative instead of collapsing to a few hub blobs.
ideas.novelty: Distinct from GEOCAP-RQ (popularity-sized, positive feedback, per-codeword offset added to a Poincare distance), from the holonomy two-leg transport (cross-chart, rejected), and from BRad-RQ (behaviour-rank on a radial coordinate). Here there is no popularity term at all and no additive offset: each codeword k at level l receives a geodesic cell RADIUS that is an inverse function of that level's behaviour-weighted occupancy, and the radius is computed by INVERTING the hyperbolic area law of the SAME curvature that defines the assignment distance. The curvature is trainable and appears three times in one chain (area law, exp/log chart map, geodesic distance); the exponent is derived from the area law instead of being a tuned power; and the occupancy feedback is negative (homeostatic), the opposite sign of everything tried so far.
ideas.observables: Level-wise SID diagnostics logged every epoch and at the end: level-1 hard ER, level-1 positive hit rate, level-2 distinct prefixes, l3_refinement_gain_bits, l3_collision (the Stage-3 admission gate), prefix-behaviour predictability (accuracy of a frozen small probe predicting the level-3 code from the level-1..2 prefix plus the behaviour context vector), and the logged trajectories of c_l and of the entropy of rho_{l,k} across codes per level; finally Stage3 test_recall@10, the only judgement.
risks: Inverse-occupancy radii may over-sharpen level-1 cells for very popular codes and push level-1 ER back up; the floor g>=0.05 and the negative feedback are the only guards, and they are not tuned.; The occupancy buffer is frozen per epoch, so the homeostatic loop can oscillate between epochs (code shuts, refills, shuts); EMA with a fixed documented default 0.5 is the only damping and is not swept.; Cold or rare items have degenerate successor entropy; the neutral fallback (btilde = 0 below 5 transitions) may wash out the behaviour signal exactly where SIDs are hardest.; Trainable curvature can drift to the lower clamp c -> 1e-3, which makes the run Euclidean in disguise and removes the geometric part of the coupling; the run has no geometric-off arm, so this can only be seen in the logged c_l trajectory, not repaired.; A single run and a single seed mean the l3_collision/recall margins must be large enough to survive seed noise; a marginal pass is not evidence.; Recomputing N_l every epoch depends on the previous epoch's hard assignments, so epoch 0 uses uniform radii; early codebook specialisation can lock in an unlucky partition.
ideas.safeguards: (1) Straight-through estimator kept exactly as x_q = z + (x_q - z).detach(), applied once, so the encoder cannot collapse. (2) Codebook parameterised in the tangent space at the origin and clamped, ||T_{l,k}|| <= 6/sqrt(c_l), and c_l clamped to [1e-3, 8] through kappa_l, so no point leaves the ball and no artanh diverges; Euclidean norms c||p||^2 are kept below 1 by the 0.95 boundary fraction. (3) arcosh argument clamped to >= 1 + 1e-7 and the Poincare denominator clamped to >= 1e-9 against NaN/Inf. (4) Radius clipped to [0.05, 0.98] * R_ref so no cell is zero or degenerate, and empty codes legitimately get the maximum radius and refill (self-healing, negative feedback). (5) Laplace-style floor on the occupancy weight, clip(1+btilde, 0.05, 4), keeps weights strictly positive and bounded, and items with fewer than 5 training transitions get btilde = 0. (6) N_l and s_l are stop-gradient buffers rebuilt once per epoch from train items only, with the documented default EMA 0.5 damping s_l; epoch 0 uses uniform N_l and p = 0.5. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
